content.title: Explainable, Site-Specific Anomaly Detection for ProtoSense

facts.text: ArmaturaSec reports several terabytes of client captures collected over three years, but no confirmed attack captures. Some clients previously lacked monitoring; the company acknowledges that compromise could have gone unnoticed.

sources.quote: we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years
we have zero examples of malicious traffic
A few of them have been running their networks for twenty years with no security monitoring at all, so if they were compromised they would not know.

facts.text: ProtoSense covers Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. ArmaturaSec reports that its previous classifier's false positives caused clients to disable alerts. Its account discusses site-specific baselines and plain-language communication with plant managers.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site
We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

facts.text: The company reports hardware for on-device inference and an Embedded Linux, C and Rust environment. Its hardware plan links anomaly detection to unchanged packet-forwarding latency.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
C and Rust for firmware components
support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

facts.text: ArmaturaSec states a collaboration capacity of one to two part-time engineers and names traffic archives, a hardware bench and its firmware codebase as resources under an NDA framework.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

facts.text: Kiss’s Modbus research models per-register timing, values and command sequences. Her incremental modelling work also tested operator-acknowledged resets after planned process reconfiguration.

sources.quote: For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated
Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode;
a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested.

facts.text: Kiss’s group operates an ICS testbed with Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators. Her notes identify a data-sharing agreement as the framework for industrial testbed access.

sources.quote: Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

facts.text: Kiss lists joint projects with ICS monitoring companies among her collaboration interests. Her review discusses a false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
the trade-off between false alarm rate and response latency.

inferences: This suggests a practical joint project combining interpretable statistical baselines with one-class modelling. Participation remains conditional because Kiss’s availability is unknown, despite her stated openness to joint projects.
The supplied work does not establish BACnet validity or ProtoSense hardware compatibility. Transfer testing is therefore central; injected scenarios cannot establish real-world attack recall.

Unnoticed compromise could contaminate training, while maintenance could trigger nuisance alerts. Automatic adaptation might absorb persistent attacks; restrictive updates could increase alert burden. The reported false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff is a deployment risk.
proposedActions: Propose a six-week pilot. ArmaturaSec would supply authorised Modbus and BACnet captures, bench replay and firmware integration; Kiss would design features and evaluation. Separate unlabelled, presumed-normal training, tuning and later held-out periods; check independence and operating-mode coverage. Compare fixed-threshold rules with statistical and one-class baselines, training and calibrating without attack labels. Select the best configuration on tuning data, whichever method wins; evaluate separately per protocol on held-out client replay and controlled bench anomalies, including BACnet-specific commands and legitimate changes. Proposed go/no-go: at least 80% of fully annotated injected episodes detected within 60 seconds of onset; the alert-burden criterion below; at least 80% correct identification of changed behaviour and appropriate next action by representative plant managers; agreed CPU, RAM, storage and throughput limits; and no measurable forwarding-latency increase under representative peak load at agreed measurement resolution. Missing protocol data, permissions or sufficient evidence leaves acceptance unresolved.

Propose counting all alert episodes, merging flagged non-overlapping ten-second windows within each site/protocol when gaps are at most 60 seconds. Divide by observed site/protocol-days; require an upper 95% day-block-bootstrap bound of one episode/day separately per protocol, retaining unresolved alerts. Randomly sample all evaluation windows uniformly, including non-alert windows, with inclusion probability n/N, for expert review. Labels would not estimate this all-alert rate; detection claims would use only fully annotated injected or confirmed cases. Insufficient exposure cannot pass.

Negotiate the NDA, client permissions and testbed data-sharing agreement within the stated part-time capacity. Benchmark the actual appliance and integrate through its Yocto/C/Rust environment rather than assuming hardware fit from published results. Use plant-manager explanation testing and expert window review, with unresolved labels treated as potentially anomalous rather than clean. Require operator approval for baseline resets and test whether persistent injected anomalies are silently learned away.
questions: Can Kiss confirm availability, implementation responsibilities and a feasible budget and schedule for this joint project?
Which appliance, resource limits, peak traffic conditions and measurement resolution will define the forwarding-latency test?
Can authorised captures for both protocols, BACnet-capable bench equipment and documented operating changes be made available under agreed confidentiality and data-sharing terms?
Can ArmaturaSec nominate expert reviewers and representative plant managers, and confirm or revise the proposed alert-burden, detection-delay and explanation criteria?

content.markdown:
# Explainable, Site-Specific Anomaly Detection for ProtoSense

## Verified facts
- ArmaturaSec reports several terabytes of client captures collected over three years, but no confirmed attack captures. Some clients previously lacked monitoring; the company acknowledges that compromise could have gone unnoticed. [F1]
- ProtoSense covers Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. ArmaturaSec reports that its previous classifier's false positives caused clients to disable alerts. Its account discusses site-specific baselines and plain-language communication with plant managers. [F2]
- The company reports hardware for on-device inference and an Embedded Linux, C and Rust environment. Its hardware plan links anomaly detection to unchanged packet-forwarding latency. [F3]
- ArmaturaSec states a collaboration capacity of one to two part-time engineers and names traffic archives, a hardware bench and its firmware codebase as resources under an NDA framework. [F4]
- Kiss’s Modbus research models per-register timing, values and command sequences. Her incremental modelling work also tested operator-acknowledged resets after planned process reconfiguration. [F5]
- Kiss’s group operates an ICS testbed with Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators. Her notes identify a data-sharing agreement as the framework for industrial testbed access. [F6]
- Kiss lists joint projects with ICS monitoring companies among her collaboration interests. Her review discusses a false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could establish whether site-specific detection produces manageable, understandable alerts on both protocols without compromising appliance operation, and identify unresolved deployment barriers.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement, Kiss could investigate transfer from established Modbus methods to BACnet and operational hardware, using authorised longitudinal captures and controlled bench scenarios to study calibration, drift and explanation quality.

## Our inference
- This suggests a practical joint project combining interpretable statistical baselines with one-class modelling. Participation remains conditional because Kiss’s availability is unknown, despite her stated openness to joint projects.
- The supplied work does not establish BACnet validity or ProtoSense hardware compatibility. Transfer testing is therefore central; injected scenarios cannot establish real-world attack recall.
- Unnoticed compromise could contaminate training, while maintenance could trigger nuisance alerts. Automatic adaptation might absorb persistent attacks; restrictive updates could increase alert burden. The reported false-alarm versus response-latency tradeoff is a deployment risk.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a six-week pilot. ArmaturaSec would supply authorised Modbus and BACnet captures, bench replay and firmware integration; Kiss would design features and evaluation. Separate unlabelled, presumed-normal training, tuning and later held-out periods; check independence and operating-mode coverage. Compare fixed-threshold rules with statistical and one-class baselines, training and calibrating without attack labels. Select the best configuration on tuning data, whichever method wins; evaluate separately per protocol on held-out client replay and controlled bench anomalies, including BACnet-specific commands and legitimate changes. Proposed go/no-go: at least 80% of fully annotated injected episodes detected within 60 seconds of onset; the alert-burden criterion below; at least 80% correct identification of changed behaviour and appropriate next action by representative plant managers; agreed CPU, RAM, storage and throughput limits; and no measurable forwarding-latency increase under representative peak load at agreed measurement resolution. Missing protocol data, permissions or sufficient evidence leaves acceptance unresolved.
- Propose counting all alert episodes, merging flagged non-overlapping ten-second windows within each site/protocol when gaps are at most 60 seconds. Divide by observed site/protocol-days; require an upper 95% day-block-bootstrap bound of one episode/day separately per protocol, retaining unresolved alerts. Randomly sample all evaluation windows uniformly, including non-alert windows, with inclusion probability n/N, for expert review. Labels would not estimate this all-alert rate; detection claims would use only fully annotated injected or confirmed cases. Insufficient exposure cannot pass.
- Negotiate the NDA, client permissions and testbed data-sharing agreement within the stated part-time capacity. Benchmark the actual appliance and integrate through its Yocto/C/Rust environment rather than assuming hardware fit from published results. Use plant-manager explanation testing and expert window review, with unresolved labels treated as potentially anomalous rather than clean. Require operator approval for baseline resets and test whether persistent injected anomalies are silently learned away.

## Open questions
- Can Kiss confirm availability, implementation responsibilities and a feasible budget and schedule for this joint project?
- Which appliance, resource limits, peak traffic conditions and measurement resolution will define the forwarding-latency test?
- Can authorised captures for both protocols, BACnet-capable bench equipment and documented operating changes be made available under agreed confidentiality and data-sharing terms?
- Can ArmaturaSec nominate expert reviewers and representative plant managers, and confirm or revise the proposed alert-burden, detection-delay and explanation criteria?
